question_fit: partly: the file can show the annual number of pedestrians injured or killed in Brooklyn police-reported crashes from 2013 onward, but it has no pedestrian travel or population exposure measure to establish risk per trip or whether safety itself improved.
metric: Annual pedestrian casualties, calculated as the sum of number_of_pedestrians_injured plus number_of_pedestrians_killed on Brooklyn crash records.
denominator: No denominator; annual count of reported pedestrian casualties.
population: Pedestrian injuries and deaths recorded on Brooklyn police-reported motor vehicle crash records, aggregated by full calendar year from 2013 through 2025.
filters: both pedestrian injury and death fields are nonmissing
years: Complete calendar years 2013–2025; the partial 2026 year is excluded.

data_check_findings.population: 483,501 Brooklyn crash records from 2013 onward; 2026 has 9,700 rows but covers only 2026-01-01 through 2026-06-11, so 2026 is excluded. Each year 2013–2025 has dates spanning January 1 through December 31.
data_check_findings.columns: After trimming and case normalization, Brooklyn matches are uppercase in the file; among the planned Brooklyn records, borough, crash_date, number_of_pedestrians_injured, and number_of_pedestrians_killed have zero missing/empty/unknown/default cases. Both outcome fields are nonmissing in all 483,501 eligible rows.
data_check_findings.change: Changed borough matching from a literal title-case comparison to case-insensitive trimmed matching after the initial literal check returned no rows. Excluded the 9,700 rows in partial 2026; retained all 2013–2025 Brooklyn rows because both outcome fields are complete.

limitations: This is an annual count, not a pedestrian risk rate: the file has no pedestrian travel-volume or population denominator. It includes police-reported crashes only, and the partial 2026 data are excluded.
